summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, possibly due to sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, was admitted with several days of worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting consistent with acute on chronic pancreatitis. She had not responded well to her usual nitroglycerin therapy. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV Dilaudid for pain, with Reglan for nausea. Over the course of the admission, her symptoms improved, and she transitioned to oral pain medication and a regular diet. Imaging showed conflicting results: MRCP suggested chronic pancreatitis with ductal changes, while EUS was normal. A sphincterotomy was not performed due to risks, and the patient was referred for a second opinion with an outside gastroenterologist. She was discharged home with instructions to resume her prior medications, maintain a low-fat diet, and follow up closely.
